"Steering Large Language Models Between Code Execution" arxiv

sources_considered.why: The May 2025 version compares text-only reasoning and code-interpreter systems across diverse reasoning and planning tasks.
Read with read_page. Its AIME results provide a narrower mathematical example, but do not independently establish breadth across task families.
Search identified relevant earlier work, but its original 2024 experiments are outside the selected observation period.

evidence_items.locator: Section 2, Task benchmark; supporting comparisons in Sections 4 and 5.1
evidence_items.explanation: The reported evaluation covers 144 tasks, including 37 held-out task types. On those held-out tasks, GPT-4o scores 58.6% with text-only reasoning and 70.9% with Code Interpreter; the trained R1-CI systems also improve across model sizes.

unresolved_gaps: The study does not establish how frequently tools help across all real-world tasks.
The R1-CI comparisons change training as well as tool use; the GPT-4o comparison provides the cleaner within-model evidence.
